--Petitioner
 Versus
Uttarakhand Rural Roads Development Agency & Others 
--Respondents
Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C. J.
Hon’ble Subhash Upadhyay, J.
1. Mr. Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for the 
petitioner.
2. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the 
respondents.
3. The petitioner made complaint against 
respondent no.6 that the vehicles offered by him for 
undertaking the contract work were in fact registered 
against a person different from one who had given 
undertaking by way of affidavit to lease out his 
vehicles. The department has simply rejected the 
complaint, observing that it is not acceptable without 
disclosing any reason therefor.
4. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the 
department seeks time to obtain instructions.
5. As prayed by him, put up as fresh on 
25.09.2026.
6. Meanwhile, the petitioner is permitted to serve 
dasti summons on respondent no.6 and file an 
affidavit of service.
(Subhash Upadhyay, J.)(Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)

25.09.2026 UKHC010167212026

Hon’ble Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.
Hon’ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
1. Mr. K.K. Harbola, learned counsel holding brief of Mr. 
Bhagwat Mehra, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for respondent 
nos.1 to 5.
3. Mr. Tribhuwan Chandra Pandey, learned counsel for 
respondent no.6.
4. Mr. S.S. Chauhan, learned counsel for the respondent￾Department could not explain how the affidavit given by 
respondent no.6 to demonstrate that he had the requisite 
machinery available with him to perform the work, if 
granted, could have been accepted when the deponent of 
the affidavit is not the registered owner of the vehicle.
5. Let counter-affidavit be filed within two weeks.
6. List immediately thereafter.
7. Meanwhile, no further action shall be taken in 
pursuance of the tender process, in question.
 (Pankaj Purohit, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
